verdict.line: You lose if you trade autos into his stacking Hemorrhage before level 6, you win once Counter Strike is up often enough to punish every Apprehend.

brief.thesis: Darius wants long auto-attack exchanges that stack Hemorrhage toward the enrage threshold, and early on his Apprehend (E, 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s cooldown) plus Crippling Strike (W) slow lets him force those exchanges. Jax's answer, Counter Strike (E, 18/16/14/12/10s cooldown), dodges his autos entirely and stuns him afterward, but at rank 1 it's too slow to be up for every engage. The lane belongs to whoever plays the cooldown gap: bait his E, and Jax's 52.9% win rate over 261 games and solo-kill edge take over.

tell.watch: Darius's Hemorrhage stack count on you

theirWindow.what: He can hook you in from 535 range, land Crippling Strike to lock the slow, and stack Q/auto bleed toward enrage. Don't extend trades or stand at his hook range while his E is up.

yourWindow.when: his Apprehend just whiffed or is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Walk up and use Counter Strike immediately — you dodge his next auto during the stance, then stun him when it resolves. Empower with W into the stun for the bonus damage, then Leap Strike away before he can start a fresh bleed stack. Respect that Decimate (Q) still has a 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown wind-up even with his E down.

playing.title: Bait Apprehend before you commit
playing.detail: Don't walk into hook range while his E is up. Once it's down (26s at rank 1, dropping to 16s late), that's your multi-second window to walk up and start the fight on your terms, per the standard read on this matchup.

playing.title: Count bleed stacks, not just his HP
playing.detail: Hemorrhage stacks to 5 and enrages him with massive bonus AD at max stacks — disengage before he caps it out, especially once you're both mid-trade.

playing.title: Trade into the stun, not around it
playing.detail: Counter Strike dodges his next incoming auto during the stance and only stuns once it resolves — time your E for right after he swings, not before, so you don't waste the dodge window.

playing.title: Leap Strike to reset, not to open
playing.detail: Use Q after your Counter Strike stun to disengage or reposition rather than as your opening move — its 17s cooldown at rank 1 is too long to burn before the fight starts.

playing.title: Play the wave passively levels 1-3
playing.detail: This is his window; freeze or shove to turret rather than trading freely until your E cooldown is short enough to answer every Apprehend.

playing.title: All-in off level 6
playing.detail: Once your ultimate is up, extended attack-speed trades favor you — look to force fights right as his Apprehend goes down.

playing.title: Empower into your stun window
playing.detail: Hold W (Empower) until Counter Strike lands its stun so the bonus damage guarantees a hit instead of risking it on a dodgeable auto.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the cooldown reads, trade timing, and stack-watching advice are my own tactical judgment layered on top.
